headline: Every major still above its 200-day, and every major red on the day
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's the strangest split in this data: all seven majors sit above their 12-month highs by wide margins (BTC -38.9%, ETH -48.5%, SOL -60.1%), yet BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and BNB are all still above their 200-day line with golden crosses intact. DOGE and ADA are the exceptions, both below their 200-day and without a golden cross. That's a market where the long-term trend structure for most of the majors is still constructive even as the last 24 hours look ugly across the board: every single asset in this set is down on the day, led by ETH at -3.95% and SOL at -3.72%. The week tells the same story as the day (BTC -4.6%, BNB -6.4%, DOGE -9.4%), but the month is the opposite (BTC +20.0%, SOL +34.3%, ETH +30.0%). Three windows, three different pictures. Treat that as three separate facts, not one trend.

Momentum is oddly calm for a day like this. RSI-14 readings sit in a tight 45-56 band across the board, essentially neutral, neither overbought nor broken. MACD is below signal on every asset, which flags fading upside momentum, but with RSI this centered it reads more like a cooling-off than a rollover. Total market cap fell 5.23% in 24 hours while individual majors fell 2-4%, meaning the smaller names in the broader index took a harder hit than BTC or ETH did, consistent with the movers list where RAY, INJ and FIL each dropped over 11% while a handful of names like ARB and FF ran the other way.

Positioning is where it gets interesting. BTC funding on OKX is a modest 0.007% per 8 hours (7.7% annualized), positive but not hot, and BTC's long/short ratio of 1.81 shows more accounts leaning long than short. ETH and SOL funding are both slightly negative (-1.0% and -2.8% annualized) despite long/short ratios above 2, meaning shorts are getting paid to hold their side even though longs outnumber them, a real divergence between crowd positioning and the cost of that positioning. DOGE stands out with a long/short ratio of 4.77 and positive funding of 5.3% annualized, a crowded long book, and it also posted the worst liquidation skew: $584,620 in long liquidations against just $29,802 in shorts over 2 hours. BTC's liquidations ran the other way, $1.16M in shorts wiped out with zero long liquidations in the same window, which lines up with a down day squeezing whoever was short.

Flows disagree with each other in a way worth sitting with. BTC spot ETFs posted a $159.9M net inflow on 14 Sep 2026, but the five-session net for BTC ETFs is a $302.8M outflow, and same_direction_days of 1 confirms that single green day breaks a run of red ones. ETH ETFs are cleaner: $121.1M inflow on the same day, $318.0M net inflow over five sessions, two days running the same direction. Meanwhile whale wallets moved $48.2M net onto exchanges in the last 24 hours, with BTC alone contributing $76.9M onto Binance (partly offset by CRO moving off exchanges). Zoom out on the weekly whale series and the direction has been onto exchanges for four straight weeks: $1,094M (week ending Aug 25), $49M, $290M, and $674M (week ending Sep 15). Coins moving toward exchanges in size, alongside a red day in spot prices, is the kind of alignment that doesn't need embellishing.

Sentiment is the outlier that ties the day together: Fear & Greed sits at 69, labeled Greed, near the top of its 30-day range of 31 to 74, on a day when every major asset is down and whales are net feeding exchanges. The crowd gauge hasn't caught up to the tape. Stablecoin float is up a modest 1.35% over 30 days to $310.3B, so there's dry powder sitting on the sideline, but it isn't described as flowing in today. What's worth watching from here: whether BTC ETF flows post a second straight inflow day (same_direction_days resetting to 2 or more) after five sessions of net outflow, whether the weekly whale series breaks its four-week streak of net onto-exchange movement, and whether DOGE's crowded long book (4.77 long/short ratio, positive funding) sees another liquidation event on the long side.
